result.title: LoopSeek: Decoupling System One Search from System Two Answering for Long Video Understanding
result.summary: Long video question answering requires finding relevant evidence before reasoning over it. With a limited frame budget, single-pass frame selection can miss critical evidence, while adaptive search often relies on repeated text generation to decide where to look. We introduce LoopSeek, a framework that decouples evidence search from answer generation through a division of labor between a non-thinking System I and a generative System II. Our key insight is that search can be expressed as a sequence of small, typed decisions, allowing System I to find the evidence that System II needs. Four System I role agents navigate a tree of video windows and coordinate through probability outputs to select frames, assess evidence, and revise the search without generating text. To align search with System II, System I learns from annotated evidence on questions that System II answers correctly only from that evidence, and the verifier's evidence estimates steer the search without calling System II, which stays frozen and answers once from the selected frames. On five long-video benchmarks, with a frozen Qwen3-VL-8B reading 32 frames, LoopSeek improves average accuracy from 53.5 to 63.9 over the uniform baseline and takes 32--80\% less GPU time per question than agentic methods.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 LoopSeek，将长视频问答中的证据搜索与回答生成解耦：由不生成文本的 System I 角色代理在视频窗口树上做类型化决策来选帧和修正搜索，冻结的 System II 仅基于选定帧作答一次。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「搜索不写文本、仅输出概率决策」、证据评估与搜索修正直接关系到 LOOK/STOP 的收益成本及视觉证据筛选；可核查这种紧凑决策状态是否减少冗余计算，以及固定帧预算下的漏检与长度泛化表现。
